original_claim: "We aren't collecting real data. Our question is about mechanism, and real data wouldn't tell us values like tolerance or rewiring probability anyway. We generate a synthetic population. Opinions start uniform between 0 and 1, because that's the convention in the Deffuant and Hegselmann-Krause papers, so we can check our model against theirs, and it represents a properly mixed starting population. It isn't empirically justified, and we say so. To make sure our conclusions don't depend on it, we also try a start centred in the middle and a start that's already two-sided. The network starts as a random graph with a set average number of links, with small-world and scale-free versions as checks. The parameters are swept over ranges, never calibrated."
